records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Biology of Humans
records.description: The biology of good health and longevity; evaluation of lifestyle choices; consideration of each body system and the potential for disease and disorder.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: General Biology
records.prerequisiteText: Enrollment not allowed if credit for BIOLOGY 105 already earned or if enrolled in BIOLOGY 105.
records.description: Understanding current and future advances in biology as 'citizen scientists'.  Lecture and laboratory; not for students majoring in the life sciences. Credit not allowed for students who have already completed BIOLOGY 105.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Science and Scientific Thinking
records.description: Exploring science as a tool for understanding nature using case studies, experimentation, and data analysis. Topics range from atoms to ecosystems including physiology, inheritance, and the carbon cycle. Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences. Recommended for students with an ALEKS math placement score of less than 45%. (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 103, SCIENCE 103.)

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: General Biology Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Junior standing.  Enrollment not allowed if credit for BIOLOGY 102 already earned or if enrolled in BIOLOGY 102.
records.description: Understanding biology as a science and its effect on issues within society.  Laboratory only.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Introductory Biology: Organismal Biology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ONE of - ALEKS math placement score of 40%, MATH 100 with an S, MATH 103 or higher, BIOLOGY 103 with a C or better, BIOLOGY 102, BIOLOGY 120, 3 credits bio with lab, or transfer credit for Intermediate Algebra equivalent to MATH 101.
records.description: One semester of a two-semester sequence (BIOLOGY 106/107 or BIOLOGY 107/106) for science majors and pre-professional students. Biology of organisms; plants, animals, ecology and evolution.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Introductory Biology: Cell Biology and Genetics
records.description: First or second semester of a one-year sequence (BIOLOGY 106/107 or BIOLOGY 107/106) for science majors and pre-professional students. Cell biology and genetics of prokaryotes and eukaryotes.  Recommended preparation: 2 credits 100-level CHEM or concurrent enrollment.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Biological Perspectives on Environmental Issues
records.description: Current case studies of human interaction with the environment exploring concepts in ecology, biodiversity, global chemical cycles, and climate change.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Laboratory Experiments in Biology and Genetics
records.description: Scientific method and its application to a diverse range of biology and genetics topics and research questions.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Introductory Botany
records.description: Introduction to plant science, highlighting certain aspects of plant biology and current research and how these relate to us all in the modern world.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Genetics and Society
records.description: Genetic topics in media and daily life including human health, agriculture, ecology and forensics for the educated non-biologist.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Introduction to Nutritional Science
records.description: Information related to dietary sources of nutrients, their functions in the body, physiologic and environmental factors that govern nutrient requirements, and guidelines for optimal dietary patterns.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Evolution
records.description: Basic principles and implications of Darwinian evolution.  Credit not granted towards elective requirements for majors in the School of Biological Sciences.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Contemporary Biology
records.description: Biological information that provides a framework for understanding life processes; impact of biological information on human affairs.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Your Future in Life Sciences
records.description: Exploration of career options in biological sciences with faculty and outside speakers; guide to preparing resume and career plans. (Crosslisted course offered as SCIENCE 210, BIOLOGY 210.)

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Medical Terminology
records.description: Terms and word constructions for health care occupations; format and function of medical records.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Exploring Health Careers
records.description: Introduction to human and animal health care careers.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Preparation for the Health Care Workplace
records.description: Basic content and skills to prepare for health related internships.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Introductory Human Physiology
records.description: Basic physiological processes in humans from the cellular to the organismal level.  Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 251 and 353.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: General Genetics
records.description: Principles of modern and classical genetics. (Crosslisted course offered as MBIOS 301, BIOLOGY 301.)

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Evolutionary Biology and Diversity
records.description: Survey of evolutionary processes that influence adaptation, diversification, and the origins and history of biodiversity; applications of evolution in conservation, agriculture, and medicine.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Biology of Sex and Gender
records.description: Biological basis of sex and its relationship to body function, women and health care, and the impact of social and cultural perspectives on the experience of being female. (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 307, WGSS 307.)

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Marine Biology
records.description: Introduction to the marine environment including oceanic, near-shore and estuarine communities of organisms and their roles and interactions.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Gross and Microanatomy
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: At least 3 credits of BIOLOGY; sophomore standing; cumulative GPA 2.5 or better.
records.description: Gross and microscopic anatomy of the human body.  Recommended for pre-health care professionals only.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Principles of Animal Development
records.description: Experimental analyses of development and descriptive and comparative examination of embryology; emphasis on the chordates.  Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 301 or MBIOS 301.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Invertebrate Biology
records.description: Phylogenetic relationships, development, and functional ecology of the invertebrate animals.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy
records.description: Evolution of vertebrates and their organ systems; correlation of structural modification with function.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Principles of Conservation
records.description: Conservation of major natural resources through a biological approach; philosophical, economic, and political aspects of important conservation issues.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Systematic Botany
records.description: Identification and classification of vascular plants with emphasis on the local flora.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Human Nutrition and Health
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 102, 106, 107, 251, 315, or concurrent enrollment in BIOLOGY 251.  Credit not granted for students who have already completed BIOLOGY 233 with a grade of C or above.
records.description: Foundations in nutritional science and its relationship to human health through the application of fundamental principles of biology.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Genome Biology
records.description: Comparative analysis of genomes from bacteria to humans including methods for sequencing, genotyping, annotation of genomes, population genetics and evolution.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Introduction to Mathematical Biology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 140 with a C or better, or MATH 172 with a C or better, or MATH 182 with a C or better; BIOLOGY 101, BIOLOGY 102, BIOLOGY 106, or BIOLOGY 107.
records.description: Mathematical biology and development of mathematical modeling for solutions to problems in the life sciences. (Crosslisted course offered as MATH 340, BIOLOGY 340.)

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Comparative Physiology
records.description: Analysis of systems and integrative physiology with an emphasis on evolutionary adaptation among mammalian and non-mammalian vertebrates.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Cells
records.description: Diversity and processes at the cellular level; structure and function.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Advanced Human Physiology
records.description: Function and control at the organ-organismic level with emphasis on mammals, including humans; emphasis on human health science applications.  Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 315 or 354. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 251 and 353.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Human Anatomy for Health Occupations
records.prerequisiteText:
Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 107; CHEM 102 with a grade of C or better or CHEM 106 with
a grade of C or better.
records.description: Histology and anatomy of humans with non-cadaver-based laboratory utilizing preserved and histological specimens, models, and software.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Molecular Processes of Living Organisms
records.description: Exploration of fundamental molecular processes to encourage thinking beyond biological species in order to comprehend larger-scale biological issues and relevance for society.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Ecology of Health and Disease
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 106; CHEM 102 or 105. Enrollment in BIOLOGY 370 not allowed if credit already earned for BIOLOGY 372.
records.description: Ecology of species interactions in changing environments and how they influence human and animal health. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 370 and 372. Field trips may be required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: General Ecology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 106; CHEM 102 or 105. Enrollment in BIOLOGY 372 not allowed if credit already earned for BIOLOGY 370.
records.description: Relationship of organisms with physical and biotic components of their environment at the population, community, and ecosystem level. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 370 and 372. Field trips may be required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Stream Monitoring
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 101, 102, or 106; CHEM 101 or 105; junior standing.
records.description: Principles and methods of water quality monitoring, including habitat assessment, water chemistry, and biological assessment. Field work and independent research required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Professional Communications in Biology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Admitted to the major in Biology or Zoology.
records.description: Literature investigation, oral presentation and written reports of selected topics in biology.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Medicine as a Career
records.description: Current issues in medicine; ethical, financial, and personal aspects of medical practice.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Evolutionary Medicine
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 301.  Enrollment not allowed if credit for BIOLOGY 403 or 405 already earned or if enrolled in either BIOLOGY 403 or 405.
records.description: Modern medical issues from an evolutionary perspective, integrated with other biological fields in medical research; topics include disease diversity, immune function, the evolution of virulence, human disease management, cancer, obesity, and human mental and reproductive health issues and their management.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Plants and People
records.description: Relationships between plants and people, especially cultural and economic applications of plants.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Beneficial Microbes in Nature and Society
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 305, 370, 372, 395, 403, or 405; junior standing.
records.description: In-depth investigations of interdisciplinary topics addressing the importance of beneficial microbes to organisms, natural systems, and society from across the disciplines of microbiology, medicine, evolutionary ecology, and agricultural science.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Evolutionary Biology
records.description: The survey of evidence for evolution and operation of evolutionary processes that influence adaptation, diversification and speciation in organisms.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Principles of Organic Evolution
records.description: The evolutionary processes that influence adaptation, population differentiation, and speciation in organisms.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Contemporary Genetics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MBIOS / BIOLOGY 301 with a C or better; junior standing.
records.description: Consideration of the state-of-the-art genetic technologies and their impact on society, environment and the economy.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Plant Anatomy
records.description: Developmental anatomy and morphology of vascular plants; economic forms. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 409 and BIOLOGY 509.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Marine Ecology
records.description: The ecology and conservation of marine organisms, communities, and ecosystems.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Biology of Fishes
records.description: Evolution, identification, life history, and characteristics of important fish species.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Parasitology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 102 or BIOLOGY 106; junior standing.
records.description: Types of associations, life cycles, control, prevention, and modifications of parasites; examination of parasitic protozoa and helminths.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Plant Physiology
records.description: Water relations, mineral nutrition, photosynthesis, respiration, and growth of plants.  Recommended:  Organic chemistry.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Plant Physiology Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 420 or concurrent enrollment.
records.description: Laboratory for Biol 420.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Ornithology
records.description: Ecology, systematics, and evolution of birds. Field trips required include two Saturdays.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Mammalogy
records.description: Ecology, systematics, and evolution of mammals.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Methods of Teaching Secondary Science I
records.description: Application of learning and theory and philosophy and structure of science in teaching middle and secondary school science courses. (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 430, MBIOS 480, TCH LRN 430.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Methods of Teaching Secondary Science II
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 430, MBIOS 480, or TCH LRN 430; junior standing.
records.description: Integration of assessment, curricular, and technological tools into instruction that aligns with learning theory and the philosophy/structure of science. (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 431, MBIOS 481, TCH LRN 431.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Biology of Amphibians and Reptiles
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 106; BIOLOGY 370, BIOLOGY 372, or SOE 300.
records.description: Characteristics, evolution, and systematics; patterns of distribution; adaptive strategies; interactions between humans and amphibians and reptiles.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Animal Behavior
records.description: Biological study of animal behavior as viewed from genetic, developmental, physiological, ecological, and evolutionary perspectives.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Hormones and Behavior
records.description: Examination of the interrelationship between the endocrine system and animal behavior with an emphasis on vertebrates and a comparative approach.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Mutualism and Symbiosis
records.description: Critical evaluation of the ecology, evolution, and molecular biology of mutualism and symbiosis. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 446 and 546.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Urban Ecology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 370 or BIOLOGY 372 or SOE 300; junior standing.
records.description: The study of the ecology of humans, organisms, and their environments in urban ecosystems.  (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 455, SOE 455.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Neuroethology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 301, MBIOS 303, or 300-level NEUROSCI course; STAT 412 or concurrent enrollment.
records.description: Introduction to neural mechanisms underlying natural animal behaviors from the cellular level to the organismal level.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Community Ecology
records.description: Assembly, essential properties, levels of interactions, succession, and stability of natural communities; emphasizes an experimental approach to community investigation. Recommended preparation:  BIOLOGY 372. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 462 and BIOLOGY 562.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Field Stream Ecology
records.description: Ecological roles of immature insects in different size streams; pattern changes along the stream continuum; other ecological characteristics.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Ecosystem Ecology and Global Change
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 370 with a C or better or BIOLOGY 372 with a C or better.
records.description: Historic and current factors controlling the function of ecosystems and their responses to natural and human caused global change.  Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 469 and 569.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Diversity of Plants
records.description: Morphological, life history, and ecological diversity of major plant clades; emphasis on principles of homology, character transformation, and macroevolution.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Evolution and Society
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ANTH 260 or BIOLOGY 301; junior standing.
records.description: Survey of how the theory of evolution is used to better understand ourselves, the societies in which live, and the biological world on which we depend. Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 305, 395, 403, or 405 or concurrent enrollment. (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 473, ANTH 473.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Computational Biology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 301; MATH 140 or 171; STAT 212, 412, or PSYCH 311.
records.description: Theory and current literature on a wide range of computational techniques used to address and solve problems in biology; a practical introduction to R/python as scientific languages useful in the solution of problems in biology.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Systems Biology of Reproduction
records.description: Current literature based course on systems biology with a molecular/epigenetic to physiological level understanding of cell, development, disease, and evolutionary biology. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 475 and 575.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Epigenetics and Systems Biology
records.description: Current literature based course on epigenetics and systems biology with topics in environmental epigenetics, disease etiology, and role epigenetics in evolutionary biology. Credit not granted for both BIOLOGY 476 and 576.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Organisms and Global Change
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 370, BIOLOGY 372, or SOE 300.
records.description: Interaction between organisms and global change across scales of biology.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Biology of the Oceans
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 370 or 372; junior standing.
records.description: Interdisciplinary capstone course that explores the ocean world from molecules to ecosystems in the context of scientific discovery and society.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Marine Invertebrate Communities
records.description: Survey of marine invertebrates and their habitats. One-week field/lab course at a marine station.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Synthesis and Communication of Independent Research
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite:  By department permission only; 2 credits BIOLOGY 499; admitted to major in Biology or Zoology; junior standing.
records.description: Integration of broad topics from biology and other science fields to inform scientific writing and presentation of independent research projects.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Professional Seminar in Physical Therapy
records.description: Consideration of treatment modalities and health issues in physical therapy and related disciplines.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Clinical Experience
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: By instructor permission; BIOLOGY 106, 107, and 221; junior standing.
records.description: Work experience in a clinical setting.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Seminar in Mathematical Biology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 140 with a C or better, or MATH 172 with a C or better, or MATH 182 with a C or better; BIOLOGY 101, BIOLOGY 102, BIOLOGY 106, or BIOLOGY 107.
records.description: Oral presentation of research approaches, research results and literature review of mathematical biology including mathematical modeling of biological systems. (Crosslisted course offered as MATH 494, BIOLOGY 494.)

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Internship in Biology, Botany, and Zoology
records.description: Experience in work related to specific career interests.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Special Problems and Reports
records.description: Independent project with written project proposal, progress report, and final report required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Instructional Practicum
records.description: Academic traineeship in laboratory teaching and tutoring.

records.subject: BIOLOGY
records.title: Special Problems
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
